market_summary: US stocks ended Oct 7 slightly lower after Tuesday's records: S&P 500 7,801.77 (-0.22%, +1.0% since Oct 2), Nasdaq 27,538.69 (-0.22%, +1.3%), Dow 51,179.87. The 10-year hit 5.365% on Oct 7, the highest since April 2002 (30-year 5.732%), then eased to about 5.28-5.31% after a $39B note auction; the Fed minutes showed all participants backed the September hike to 3.75-4.00% but split between 1-2 more hikes and an immediate pause, and futures price only about 20% for another hike on Oct 28 after 3.0% core PCE and 29K payrolls. Brent settled at $100.20 and WTI $88.28 (-1.3%); ISM services prices paid hit 74.0, the highest since July 2022, and OPEC+ held November output flat on Oct 4. AI hardware news remains strong (Samsung Q3 profit 107.4T won on Oct 8, Marvell's $70-90B FY31 target on Oct 6) while GPU rental indexes keep making highs (H100 $2.81), so the pressure on AI/Internet names is the cost of capital rather than demand. DXY and the China reopening reaction on Oct 8 were not verified (DXY was 101.92 on Oct 2). Next: TSMC September sales and China's reopening Thu Oct 8; ASML bookings and US CPI Wed Oct 14 (AEDT Thu morning); TSMC Q3 results Oct 15.

AMZN.reason: Up about 3.3% since Oct 2 and 1.4% on Oct 7 as the market slipped from records; Tigress raised its target to $385 on AI, cloud and ads. Prime Big Deal Days ran Oct 6-7 with no results published yet, and Q3 earnings are due around Oct 29, so no change.

AXOS.reason: Down 1.4% since Oct 2 and 1.5% on Oct 7 as the 10-year yield hit 24-year highs. No company news; fiscal Q1 results are due Oct 29 after the close, so nothing to act on before then.

BABA.reason: Up 1.1% since Oct 2 but down 2.1% on Oct 7, after a 4.7% jump on Oct 5 on AI cloud momentum (cloud and AI revenue up 45% last quarter). The class-action lead-plaintiff deadline passed Oct 5 with no ruling; wait for China policy and the Nov 24 earnings.

ENPH.reason: Flat over the period (down 1.2% on Oct 7) with more target cuts: Barclays to $44, Oppenheimer to $55, and Deutsche Bank named it a short-term sell into Q3 results on safe-harbor revenue risk. Stay on watch until the print.

FIGR.reason: Down 3.0% since Oct 2 though up 1.2% on Oct 7. Preliminary Q3 marketplace volume of $5.1B (up 107% year on year) hit the high end of guidance; Goldman and BofA trimmed targets to $41 and $44 but kept Buy, so hold.

GOOGL.reason: Up 2.0% since Oct 2 and 0.8% on Oct 7, the steadiest mega-cap. A 20-year Constellation nuclear power deal and Unity gaming tie-up add to the AI buildout; the Finland data-centre construction stop (by Oct 23) is a delay to a $15B plan, not a thesis change.

LDI.reason: Down about 3% since Oct 2 and flat on Oct 7, still a sub-dollar stock with an NYSE compliance notice. Mortgage rates are at their highest in about a year, so there is no near-term catalyst; keep trimming into strength.

META.reason: Down 0.9% since Oct 2 and 2.4% on Oct 7, the weakest mega-cap on the day despite the Muse iPad launch and a Citi note seeing Muse as a $27B business by 2030. Florida filed to force teen-safety changes on top of the New Mexico penalty claim; hold rather than add.

MRVL.reason: Up 4.6% since Oct 2 after a 5.8% jump on investor day and a 0.8% pullback on Oct 7. Management targets $20B revenue in FY28 and $70-90B in FY31, and about 15 brokers raised targets (Morgan Stanley and Goldman stay neutral); at roughly 60x forward earnings, hold and do not chase.

MU.reason: Up 1.2% since Oct 2, with a 4.1% rise on Oct 7 despite a Taiwan plant strike vote and a morning sell-off in memory names. D.A. Davidson set a Street-high $3,000 target; the strike has no date and the Netlist patent dispute settled, so hold.

NFLX.reason: Up 3.9% since Oct 2 and 1.5% on Oct 7, a partial bounce after the 14% September drop. Barclays cut its target to $70 from $80 ahead of Q3; the print is the next test.

NVDA.reason: Up 1.5% since Oct 2 but down 0.7% on Oct 7, just under its record. Microsoft and Dell launched RTX Spark PCs, a new consumer channel, while concentration and yield risk grow; hold.

RKT.reason: Down 2.2% since Oct 2 and 1.3% on Oct 7 as the 30-year mortgage rate index reached 7.59%, near its 52-week high. Mortgage stocks need a sustained fall in yields, which is not happening, so watch.

TSM.reason: Flat since Oct 2 after a 2.8% jump on Oct 5 and a 2.1% drop on Oct 7 when Musk said TSMC will not run his Terafab complex. Citi raised its target and expects a Q3 beat on Oct 15; September revenue is not yet out, so keep adding on weakness.

STRIPE.reason: No closed round or tender since the February tender at a $159B valuation. A secondary-market quote implies a higher figure, but that is not a closed deal, so the mark is unchanged.

OPENAI.reason: Reports from Sep 29 to Oct 6 say OpenAI is in early talks for a $30B round at about $1.4T pre-money, with MGX and BlackRock; it is not closed and has no lead investor. The mark stays until a round or tender is confirmed.

headlines: 10-year yield hit 5.365% Wednesday, highest since 2002; S&P 500 and Nasdaq slipped 0.2% from Tuesday's records.
Marvell targets $70-90B revenue in FY31; shares jumped about 6% on investor day Oct 6.
Samsung forecasts record Q3 operating profit of 107.4T won on HBM4; Micron rose 4% Wednesday.
Fed minutes: all backed September's hike, split on more. December hike odds about 85%, October about 17%.
Pentagon says it has stopped using Anthropic products, a new IPO risk; investor session Oct 14.
Next: TSMC September sales Thu, then ASML bookings and US CPI on Oct 14.
